title: Does a concept probe detect deception even when the chain-of-thought hides it?

original_idea.body: Construct prompts inducing deceptive answers with innocuous CoT, run a CoT-reading judge and a deception probe, and compare detection on the subset where the CoT does not reveal the deception.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: probes catching deception that CoT-judges miss is the core case for internal monitoring against unfaithful CoT.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probe vs judge on hidden-deception prompts; eliciting reliable hidden-CoT deception adds difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable though dataset construction is nontrivial.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Internal-monitoring case on unfaithful-CoT failure mode labs underweight; foundational.

novelty.reasoning: Probe-vs-judge on CoT-hidden deception appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: A fresh angle on internal monitoring.
